```{julia}
#| include: false
using PatternQ, DataFrames, Statistics
```

The basic patternq workflow, step by step. The same steps, with the same
datasets and outputs, are in `tutorial.qmd` in [patternq-r](https://github.com/RCRF/patternq-r) (R, knitr),
`tutorial.qmd` in [patternq](https://github.com/RCRF/patternq) (marimo) and `tutorial.clj` in [patternq-clj](https://github.com/RCRF/patternq-clj) (Clay).

| step | what |
|---|---|
| 1 | connect and find a dataset |
| 2 | explore a dataset: assays, measurement sets, samples, subjects |
| 3 | write a Datalog query |
| 4 | canned queries: variants and gene expression |
| 5 | any measurement, reshaped and joined with sample context |
| 6 | clinical outcomes and survival |
| 7 | a sample against a reference cohort |
| 8 | expression change between two samples |

## 1. Connect and find a dataset

Set `PATTERNQ_API_KEY` (and optionally `PATTERNQ_ENDPOINT`) in the environment,
or call `set_token()` / `set_query_server()`.

```{julia}
using PatternQ, DataFrames
println(query_server())
datasets = list_datasets()
first(datasets[:, [:dataset, :db, :patient_count, :sample_count]], 6)
```

Every dataset is its own database. Dataset names are stable; database names
change when a dataset is re-imported, so resolve them:

```{julia}
h37001 = resolve_db("H37001")
uvm = resolve_db("tcga-uvm")
set_db(h37001)
(h37001, uvm)
```

## 2. Explore a dataset

```{julia}
display(dataset_summary())
display(measurement_types("RSEM RNASeq"))
display(samples())
subjects()
```

## 3. Write a Datalog query

Queries are Datomic Datalog in the query service's JSON form: variables are
`"?x"`, attributes `":ns/name"`, each clause a vector.

```{julia}
q = Dict(":find" => ["?sample-id", "?site"],
         ":where" => [["?s", ":sample/id", "?sample-id"],
                      ["?s", ":sample/freetext-anatomic-site", "?site"]])
do_query(q)
```

Inputs bind with `:in` / `args`; a vector binds a collection:

```{julia}
q = Dict(":find" => ["?sample-id", "?hgnc", "?vaf"],
         ":in" => [["?hgnc", "..."]],
         ":where" => [["?g", ":gene/hgnc-symbol", "?hgnc"],
                      ["?v", ":variant/gene", "?g"],
                      ["?m", ":measurement/variant", "?v"],
                      ["?m", ":measurement/vaf", "?vaf"],
                      ["?m", ":measurement/sample", "?s"],
                      ["?s", ":sample/id", "?sample-id"]])
r = do_query(q; args=[["BAP1", "GNAQ", "SF3B1"]])
```

Every result records where it came from:

```{julia}
provenance(r)
```

## 4. Variants and gene expression

```{julia}
v = variants()
println(nrow(v), " variant measurements")
display(first(v[coalesce.(v.impact .== "high", false), [:sample_id, :hgnc_symbol, :HGVSp, :vaf]], 6))
plot_vaf_histogram(v; samples=["H37001-001", "H37001-006"])
```

```{julia}
gx = gene_expression(genes=["BAP1", "GNAQ", "PRAME", "PMEL", "MLANA"], measurement="tpm")
display(first(gx, 6))
plot_gene_expression(gx; title="Melanocytic genes (TPM)", ylab="TPM", log=true)
```

Copy number queries always take a subset (genes, samples or subjects):

```{julia}
cnv_segments(genes=["BAP1", "GNAQ"])
```

## 5. Any measurement, reshaped and joined with context

`measurements()` works for any measurement attribute and detects what each
measurement is of (gene, cell population, epitope, ...). Here: CyTOF cell
population frequencies in PRINCE.

```{julia}
prince = resolve_db("prince-2022")
display(measurement_types("PICI CyTOF Immune Profiling"; db=prince))
cy = measurements("percent-of-parent", "PICI CyTOF Immune Profiling"; db=prince)
first(cy, 6)
```

Wide (samples x populations):

```{julia}
m = to_matrix(cy, "cell_population")
size(m)
```

With sample and subject context:

```{julia}
cy = add_sample_context(cy; db=prince)
display(first(cy[:, [:sample_id, :subject_id, :timepoint_id, :cell_population, :value]], 6))
plot_by_timepoint(cy[cy.cell_population .== "HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T Cells", :];
                  timepoints=["C1D1", "C1D15", "C2D1", "C4D1"], lines=true,
                  title="HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells", ylab="% of parent")
```

## 6. Clinical outcomes and survival

```{julia}
outcomes = subject_outcomes(db=prince)
display(first(outcomes, 6))
plot_survival(outcomes; group="bor", xlab="months", title="Overall survival by best overall response")
```

Survival split at the median of a baseline biomarker, with a log-rank test:

```{julia}
base = cy[(cy.cell_population .== "HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T Cells") .& (coalesce.(cy.timepoint_id, "") .== "C1D1"), :]
baseline_values = Dict(k.subject_id => mean(g.value) for (k, g) in pairs(groupby(base, :subject_id)))
km = survival_by_median(baseline_values, outcomes)
println("log-rank p = ", metadata(km, "logrank").p)
plot_survival(km; group="group", levels=["low", "high"], xlab="months",
              title="OS by baseline HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells")
```

## 7. A sample against a reference cohort

Place a patient sample within a reference cohort's distribution, gene by gene
(z-score and percentile on log2(1 + TPM)). Only compare comparable
measurements, and check `cohort_observed`.

```{julia}
genes = ["BAP1", "GNAQ", "PRAME", "MITF", "PMEL", "TYR", "MLANA", "CD8A", "GZMB"]
cmp = compare_to_cohort("H37001-003"; db=h37001, cohort_db=uvm, genes=genes)
display(cmp[:, [:hgnc_symbol, :value, :z, :percentile, :cohort_observed]])
examine_geneset(genes, ["H37001-003", "H37001-001"]; db=h37001,
                cohort_dbs=Dict("TCGA-UVM" => uvm), title="H37001 vs TCGA-UVM")
```

## 8. Expression change between two samples

```{julia}
change = compare_samples("H37001-003", "H37001-001"; db=h37001)
display(first(change, 6))
plot_ma(change)
```
